title: Last contacts with George Lewis
summary: The interviewer's hospital visit, Green's call, and George's wish to die playing like Papa John.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes, I should just say on this tape that when I saw George in hospital just before he died, about a week before he died, I told him I was going to Washington, which I... When I left, I knew I probably wouldn't see him again. He did say, you'll see Bob Green. You'll see Bob Green when he was in Washington. He said it two or three times. He did come down, of course, before he died.
I wasn't able to. I called. There were no more visitors, but I asked that my name be left. And evidently it was. So? Well, we're all poorer. Yeah.
Yeah. Well. Okay. Well, thanks so much, Bob. Good job. That's fine. One footnote.
I visited George in October out in Darmus Street in Algiers.

Yeah. And he was ill. And he said, Bob, when I go, I hope I go like Papa John. I hope I go on the bandstand. He said, I never want to quit playing. I want to go like Papa John. Mm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
